title_vi: Khởi động Linux: tám bước của nguồn, điều tài liệu thêm vào, và một lần đọc tĩnh các tệp đơn vị systemd

claims.claim_vi: Source: eight steps - firmware (BIOS/UEFI) loaded from non-volatile memory runs POST; BIOS/UEFI detects devices (CPU, RAM, storage); choose a boot device (disk, network server, CD ROM); BIOS/UEFI runs the boot loader (GRUB); kernel starts systemd as the first user-space process; systemd activates default.target; startup scripts run; login window.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: boot(7): after power-on control is given to a program in read-only memory (the BIOS) that performs a basic self-test and reads parameters from non-volatile memory, which name the boot device; the OS loader (often lilo or grub) locates and loads the kernel and passes parameters; the kernel initializes components, mounts a root filesystem and only then creates the first user-land process with PID 1, traditionally executing /sbin/init; the System V init and /etc/init.d scripts are described as System V Release 4 specific.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of man-pages at commit ae6b221882ce71ba82fcdbe02419a225111502f0.

claims.claim_vi: bootup(7): firmware does minimal hardware initialization and hands control to a boot loader (systemd-boot or GRUB), which invokes the kernel; EFI firmware may also load the kernel directly; the kernel may mount an in-memory file system (initramfs) that finds the root file system; then the system manager (such as systemd) on the root file system probes the remaining hardware, mounts file systems and spawns services; systemd activates the units that are dependencies of default.target, usually an alias of graphical.target or multi-user.target; boot is highly parallelized so the order in which targets are reached is not deterministic.
claims.verified_by: File downloaded from systemd at commit cb070c87eb12f3cf1f85873db38ff756a111460e on 2026-10-19.

claims.claim_vi: Static reading of unit files on a systemd 255 installation: default.target links to graphical.target; following Requires, Wants, BindsTo, Requisite and .wants/.requires directories gives 78 units (35 services, 18 targets, 8 timers, 7 sockets, 6 mounts, 2 paths, 1 automount, 1 slice), 11 names with no file; 94 explicit After/Before edges inside the set; longest chain of explicitly declared ordering 15 units; 41 of 78 units declare no wait on another unit of the set (systemd also adds synthesized ordering from DefaultDependencies=yes, from the Wants/Requires of target units and implicit dependencies of mounts, sockets and paths, which this reading does not model, so the figures are not the actual boot ordering); sysinit.target pulls 41 units; PID 1 of the machine is not systemd although /sbin/init links to systemd.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19; reads declarations only, ignores conditions and template units.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: tám bước, điều tài liệu thêm hoặc sửa, đọc tĩnh một máy thật.
source_deviations: The source is a picture with eight short steps; the lesson keeps the eight steps in order, adds the initramfs step the source lacks, and adds a static reading of unit files.
No boot was run and no boot time was measured; GRUB and UEFI documents were not read.
